After converting the survey data to the same coordinate reference system as the flood data we can look at the intersection of the two data points. # need to make some data to verify # names throw an error due to character incompatibility, so remove altogether survey_sf <- odhf_valid %>% st_as_sf(coords=c("long", "lat"), crs=st_crs(4326)) %>% select(-facility_name) %>% st_transform(st_crs(flood_data)) 4.3.3 Data Manipulation Buffer distance is easily customisable for different use cases. This chunk will loop through each of the points of interest to determine flood exposure with the floods dataset. buffer_distance = 25000 # in metres # create a buffer around each poi survey_buffered <- st_buffer(survey_sf, dist = buffer_distance) # find floods within each poi's buffer flood_matches <- st_intersects(survey_buffered, flood_data) # extract year and month from flood event datetime flood_data <- flood_data %>% mutate(flood_year = year(datetime_utc), flood_month = month(datetime_utc)) # initialize an empty data frame to store results exposure_matrix <- matrix(0, nrow = nrow(survey_sf), ncol = 25) colnames(exposure_matrix) <- paste0("month_", 0:24) #column names for each month # loop through each poi and determine flood exposure for (i in seq_len(nrow(survey_sf))) { # extract the survey date from the survey related columns survey_year <- survey_sf$survey_year[i] survey_month <- survey_sf$survey_month[i] # compute the 24-month range month_seq <- seq.Date(from = as.Date(sprintf("%d-%02d-01", survey_year, survey_month)) %m-% months(1), length.out = 24, by = "-1 month") month_seq_df <- data.frame(year = year(month_seq), month = month(month_seq)) # get the indices of intersecting floods for this poi flood_indices <- flood_matches[[i]] if (length(flood_indices) > 0) { # if floods exist in the buffer flood_events <- flood_data[flood_indices, c("flood_year", "flood_month")] # check for each of the past 24 months if a flood occurred for (j in 1:24) { target_year <- month_seq_df$year[j] target_month <- month_seq_df$month[j] # if a flood occurred in this year-month, set exposure to 1 if (any(flood_events$flood_year == target_year & flood_events$flood_month == target_month)) { exposure_matrix[i, j] <- 1 } } } } # Data can be obtained programmatically (as below), or manually for each hurricane of interest from the NOAA website. Should you choose to download the files yourself, the script is designed to use shapefiles (.shp). It is important to note that the following script should be used sparingly We first need to specify when and where the hurricane data is retrieved from. base_page <- "https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/gis/archive_besttrack.php?year=" base_zip <- "https://www.nhc.noaa.gov/gis/best_track/" hurricane_years_interest <- 2008:2025 #getting data for all years from 2008 to 2025 Next, we set up the storage location for the hurricane best track files and create a lookup table for later. It is important to set a viable output directory for the best tracks from the website. #set an output directory for the data to download into base_shape_dir <- "./data/HurricaneRawData/nhc_best_tracks" dir.create(base_shape_dir, showWarnings = FALSE) #create a lookup table for the storms that can be used later to create a connection between the storm name and data storm_summary <- data.frame(Year = integer(), Storms = integer()) storm_lookup <- data.frame(year = integer(), storm_id = character(), storm_name = character()) Finally, we get the files from the website for each year specified. Within this snippet, a lookup table for the file names and actual hurricane name is created and saved as a .csv for later reference. (TODO: add a switch to get just the names list vs. the file and names list) #process every year for the year range specified above for (year in hurricane_years_interest) { cat("processing", year, "\n") #read the page, catch if the response is blank page <- tryCatch({ read_html(paste0(base_page, year)) }, error = function(e) { cat("could not read page for", year, "\n") return(NULL) }) if (is.null(page)) next #extract all the rows on the page to get the hurricane codes and names from the table for that year rows <- html_nodes(page, "tr") #loop through rows to match "al##" and extract name from second column to create lookup table for (row in rows) { cols <- html_nodes(row, "td") #get all the td html elements if (length(cols) >= 2) { id_text <- str_trim(html_text(cols[1])) #just want the id from the td elements if (str_detect(tolower(id_text), "^al\\d{2}$")) { #regex to get the atlantic (al) storm and the id number name_text <- str_trim(html_text(cols[2])) #get the nominal identifier storm_lookup <- rbind( #collect and add to the storm loookup table storm_lookup, data.frame( #create a data frame with the year, storm id from the td element, and the storm name year = year, storm_id = tolower(id_text), storm_name = name_text, stringsAsFactors = FALSE ) ) } } } #get just the text from all the td html elements td_text <- html_text(html_nodes(page, "td"), trim = TRUE) #get the strom ids again (for redundancies sake) storm_ids <- unique(str_to_lower(str_subset(td_text, "^al\\d{2}"))) #make sure it's just the 4 character id with more regex storm_ids <- gsub("\\s.*", "", storm_ids) cat(" found", length(storm_ids), "atlantic storms\n") #storm summary for creating storm ids in file names storm_summary <- rbind(storm_summary, data.frame(Year = year, Storms = length(storm_ids))) #file naming system is regular within the website hierarchy, so download all zip shapefiles using the engineered storm names for (storm_id in storm_ids) { zip_name <- paste0(storm_id, year, "_best_track.zip") url <- paste0(base_zip, zip_name) dest <- file.path(base_shape_dir, zip_name) #set outpath based on string specified earlier cat(" downloading:", zip_name, "\n") resp <- tryCatch({ GET(url, write_disk(dest, overwrite = TRUE)) #get zip file from constructed url }, error = function(e) { cat(" failed to download", zip_name, "\n") #sometimes there are no files to download, especially in earlier years return(NULL) }) #unzip the files too, easier to do now than later if (!is.null(resp) && status_code(resp) == 200) { unzip(dest, exdir = file.path(base_shape_dir, paste0(storm_id, "_", year))) } else { cat(" file not found:", url, "\n") } #be kind to the server and don't get banned from scraping Sys.sleep(1.1) } }
